definition: The practice of taking a model trained on one task or dataset and adapting it to a different but related task, leveraging previously learned representations.
details: Transfer learning underlies the modern pretrain-then-fine-tune paradigm, allowing models to reuse general knowledge learned from large datasets rather than learning every task from scratch.
story: Think of the first time you rode a scooter after years on a bicycle. You did not start from zero — your body already knew balance and steering, so you only had to learn what was new. Computers can do the same thing: once they have learned one big skill, picking up a similar new skill takes a fraction of the effort. That is why a machine that has read a mountain of writing can quickly learn to summarize it or answer questions about it. Transfer Learning is simply the habit of carrying what you already know into the next new thing.
